subject: Crosswalk & scorecard for level mapping + geo scaling
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Benchmarks Team <benchmarks@compbench.co>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Level crosswalk & geo-scaling inputs

Hi all,

Attached is the Q2 market readout from CompBench (compbench_q2_market_readout.xlsx). Key pieces I flagged for us:

- Median base vs. market for IC3-IC6 per major metro (US/EMEA/APAC).
- Proposed local multipliers (0.82–1.35) based on cost-of-living and local competitor mixes.
- Methodology notes: blended medians weighted by cohort size and recent offers.

Ask: can the HR leveling team confirm whether a blended multiplier or a hard geo band is preferred for offer automation?

Initial suggestions from my side:
- Build a crosswalk that maps current internal bands to a normalized score (0–100) driven by comp percentile and role criticality.
- Use that score to pick a geo multiplier bucket in the offer flow.

Planning note: if we adopt a score-driven approach we can pilot in LATAM and one APAC city to measure offer acceptance delta.

I'll be available all day Friday for a quick sync.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, People Analytics
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level crosswalk & geo-scaling inputs

Thanks Jonas — helpful deck and data. I reviewed the attachment and sketched a lightweight scorecard to operationalize the crosswalk (attached: leveling_scorecard_v1.xlsx).

High level responses and follow-ups:

1) Score dimensions: I propose three axes: Market Percentile (base comp vs. market), Role Scarcity (1–5), and Internal Anchor (how far role is from current internal median). Weighted: 50/30/20.

2) Output: a normalized score -> mapped to one of five geo buckets (A–E). Each bucket has a defined multiplier and a max uplift cap.

3) Exception flow: any uplift > 20% should trigger Manager + People Ops approval. We should codify the threshold and the approver queue in Workday/Greenhouse integration.

4) Pilot plan: run for new external offers and internal transfers in Brazil (Sao Paulo) and Singapore for 8 weeks. Objective metrics: time to offer, acceptance rate, projected comp delta, and overall cost delta to budget.

Can Stephanie and Karthik confirm capacity for the pilot (platform/integration touchpoints)? I can draft the pilot scope and a short comms note to hiring managers once design is agreed.

Next steps:
- Jonas: confirm weighting and whether CompBench can expose per-role scarcity signals (not just market percentile).
- Stephanie/Karthik: confirm pilot feasibility and any integration blockers by 08/06.
- Laura: review approval thresholds and governance language.

Thanks — I attached a short doc that outlines the pilot scope (neha_pilot_scope.docx).

Neha
People Ops Program Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level crosswalk & geo-scaling inputs

Neha — thanks, this feels like a pragmatic approach. A few clarifying points and one governance ask: 

- Uplift caps: I support a hard cap at 25% for any single offer relative to the internal anchor. For critical hires (scarcity 5) we can allow up to 35% but require Director + Head of People Ops approval.

- Retroactive adjustments: we need a policy for internal transfers that land outside the new bands. I recommend a 90-day review window with a separate budget code for one-time leveling adjustments so we don't erode existing budgets unexpectedly.

- Cost modeling: before pilot sign-off, Finance needs a ballpark estimate of cost exposure if we replaced local manual uplifts with the proposed scorecard across 4 target markets. Jonas — can you run a delta model (3-year, cohort-level) as part of the CompBench engagement?

Governance: Draft language below that I'd like included in the playbook so people know when escalations are required:

> Any calculated uplift that increases total cash comp by >25% relative to the current internal anchor requires single off-cycle approval from the Head of People Ops. Anything >35% requires Director-level pre-approval and Finance sign-off.

If we can get the scoring and the Finance model by next Wednesday (08/11) we can freeze the pilot design and schedule comms the week of 08/16.

Laura
VP, Talent & Total Rewards
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Benchmarks Team <benchmarks@compbench.co>
Date: Sun, 08 Aug 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level crosswalk & geo-scaling inputs

All — quick update after a call with CompBench and Finance:

- CompBench can provide role-level scarcity scores (yes) and will add a per-city volatility flag we can use to throttle uplifts in noisy markets.
- I ran a delta projection for four markets (US-SF, UK-LON, BR-SA, SG) and attached the output to their portal; summary: projected incremental cash spend year 1 = ~1.8% of base payroll for targeted cohorts (detailed sheet in compbench portal).
- Operationally, we will: 1) lock scorecard weights (50/30/20), 2) implement geo bucket mapping, and 3) cap automated uplift at 25% with exception paths for scarcity 5 candidates up to 35%.

Next steps:
- Neha: finalize pilot scope doc and sample comms (you mentioned 08/16 week for comms).
- Stephanie/Karthik: confirm integrations and inform Product of any API requirements to surface multiplier buckets in offer UI.
- CompBench: please share the role-level scarcity export to the Drive folder (link below).

Thanks — I'll schedule a 30-min sync for next Tuesday to freeze the pilot plan.

Jonas
